declaredRefusal.description:
One package-declared business refusal from a validated product response.

The code is deliberately absent from `Debug`; callers must opt in to reading
or serializing it for an authored refusal branch.
declaredRefusal.title: invoke-breg-action declared-refusal output

BRegActionResultReference.description: One disclosed effect reference in a successful action receipt.

GrantReference.description:
An approval reference, never an assertion or bearer credential. The shared
Casework source requires the signed authority's original deadline to match.

domainData.description: Project-defined record data. An imported BReg record schema limits member names to the record type's API names. Fields may be hidden by access policy; value types remain open. Without a record import, any member name is accepted.

RegistryRecordMeta.description:
The homogeneous Registry, primary dataset, and entity context shared by a
single response or every member of a collection.

output.description: One Registry Record v1 single-response envelope.
output.title: breg.read-record/v1 output

input.description:
The input of `cancel-review-request`: the accepted request a submit step
returned and the reason Casework records with the cancellation.
input.title: casework.cancel-review-request/v1 input

publicReason.description:
Text the decision gives for release to the subject's owner. It is
distinct from the reviewer's private reason, which never leaves
Casework.

PolicySelection.description:
Select the trusted provider's current policy, or require one exact binding.
The selector stays in the submission identity; acceptance records the concrete binding.

Question.description: Authored questions are distinct from each provider's external DTO spelling.

state.description: The evaluated state: any JSON object, string or array.

output.description:
The evaluate-decision call output. Answers keep the authored question
identifiers; usage keeps the provider's own metadata spelling.
output.title: evaluation.evaluate/v1 output

declaredRefusal.description:

declaredRefusal.title: external.command/v1 declared-refusal output

input.description: The command body, sent as the exact JSON object to the connection's configured command path.
input.title: external.command/v1 input

output.description: The bounded provider response. The operation's interpret Function receives it with the command and returns the step result, a declared refusal, or an uncertain outcome.

body.description: The parsed JSON response body, or null for an empty body.

output.title: external.command/v1 output

output.description:
The external-get call output. The body is open here: the connection's
operator-owned response schema constrains it in the runtime configuration.

body.description: The parsed JSON response body, or null for an empty body.

output.title: external.get/v1 output

DirectContent.description: Content a caller supplies instead of naming a template.

Recipient.description:
Where one message goes: exactly one email address or one E.164 phone
number, written `{"email": ...}` or `{"phone": ...}`.

Its `Debug` never prints the contact, so a recipient that reaches a log
through a derived `Debug` names only its kind.

TemplateReference.description:
One template version, under `templates/<id>/<version>/`, as the wire
contract names it.

input.description:
The body of `POST /v1/messages`. Exactly one of `template` or `content`
is present; `locale` and `data` accompany a template and nothing else.
Instants are RFC 3339 strings the runtime parses.
input.title: messaging.submit-message/v1 input

MessageLinks.description: The links a message answer carries.

MessageStatus.description:
The public status of one message, derived from its dispatch state and
its delivery report by [`derive_status`].

output.description:
The `202` answer to an accepted submission, and what a replayed key
answers again.
output.title: messaging.submit-message/v1 output

GrantReference.description:
An approval reference, never an assertion or bearer credential. The shared
Casework source requires the signed authority's original deadline to match.

AllocationDocument.description:
One concrete part of an authorized logical reservation. A counted line
may have several rows when capacity is split across members.

AllocationRequirementDocument.description: Which canonical request line produced one concrete allocation.

AppointmentStateDocument.description: The lifecycle state of an appointment on the wire.

AttendanceDocument.description: The current attendance observation for one appointment visit.

appointmentRevision.description:
The booking revision the recorder observed. A later cancellation may
advance the current booking revision without changing this fact.

revision.description: Globally monotonic within the appointment, including across visits.

AttendanceState.description:
One authorized observation about a logical appointment.

This is deliberately appointment-level. It neither identifies one person
nor derives a count from the booking party or its reserved units.

ExternalReference.description:
An opaque link to a record owned by another product.

Scheduling stores and returns this tuple without resolving it. The
identifier names only the referenced record; callers must not put personal
data in any field.

ManagerSelection.description:
An explicit selector for a source-bound managing authority.

The selector carries no identity. Scheduling resolves the fixed signed
task-grant subject of the same name and verifies its current status.

PartyCounts.description:
The declared party counts committed with a hold or appointment.

Recipients are the people the service is delivered to; attendees are
everyone expected to be present, recipients included. These values explain
a capacity decision. They are not an observation that attendance occurred,
and neither value is an inventory quantity.

PartyReference.description:
A typed reference to a party record owned by another product.

Scheduling retains this value as booking data. It proves no relationship
and grants no read or mutation authority.

PartyReferenceRole.description: The source-owned meaning of an opaque party reference.

allocations.description:
Present for a quantity or multi-line reservation. Omitted on the
legacy single-resource path.

attendance.description:
The current observation for this appointment's current visit, when an
exact-detail authority is reading it.

resource.description: The pool member serving the appointment, for exact-time offerings.

One secondary physical allocation in a logical reservation. Its displayed
interval is the primary request's interval; its offering supplies its own
occupied buffers and resource policy.

resource.description: An exact member selection. Omission requests fungible selection.

units.description: Physical resource units, independent of party counts.

resolves nothing, fetches nothing, and reads exactly what it is handed.

capabilities.description:
The party's held capability references, matched against the offering's
requirements.

channel.description:
The authenticated channel, when the deployment allocates supply
through channel subquotas.

duplicateKey.description:
The duplicate-active key, derived the same way the offering's policy
prescribes.

durationMinutes.description:
The displayed interval selected by the caller. Omitted, exact-time

admission refuses this member as out of policy.

AttendanceState.description:
One authorized observation about a logical appointment.

This is deliberately appointment-level. It neither identifies one person
nor derives a count from the booking party or its reserved units.

ExternalReference.description:
An opaque link to a record owned by another product.

Scheduling stores and returns this tuple without resolving it. The
identifier names only the referenced record; callers must not put personal
data in any field.

ManagerSelection.description:
An explicit selector for a source-bound managing authority.

The selector carries no identity. Scheduling resolves the fixed signed
task-grant subject of the same name and verifies its current status.

PartyCounts.description:
The declared party counts committed with a hold or appointment.

Recipients are the people the service is delivered to; attendees are
everyone expected to be present, recipients included. These values explain
a capacity decision. They are not an observation that attendance occurred,
and neither value is an inventory quantity.

PartyReference.description:
A typed reference to a party record owned by another product.

Scheduling retains this value as booking data. It proves no relationship
and grants no read or mutation authority.

PartyReferenceRole.description: The source-owned meaning of an opaque party reference.

allocations.description:
Present for a quantity or multi-line reservation. Omitted on the
legacy single-resource path.

attendance.description:
The current observation for this appointment's current visit, when an
exact-detail authority is reading it.

resource.description: The pool member serving the appointment, for exact-time offerings.
